subject: Request: p50/p95 banding and measurement evidence for Hosted API
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: p50/p95 banding and measurement evidence for Hosted API

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Brightline's legal team asked us to provide a short proposal that captures two items so you can review them internally:

1) A temporary banding (grace) around the p95 measurement during the migration period you mentioned (Dec 15–Jan 15). Specifically: a +25% p95 tolerance for any 7-day rolling window where we can show correlated traffic surges.

2) A concise evidence package showing our measurement method (how p50/p95 are computed, measurement window definition, sampling approach) so Brightline Legal can validate the audit trail.

Karthik — can you attach the evidence bundle and a short note on how we calculate rolling-window p95? Marissa — I'll need a one-paragraph onboarding note for operations (what to expect if the banding is accepted).

Sam — I've put the draft addendum in the attached PDF for legal to scan; it's intentionally conservative and includes an auto-revert if we detect sustained regressions.

Next step: if this looks reasonable from Brightline Legal, can we get a short approval (email) so we can add the addendum to the order form and schedule a quick ops runbook review later this week?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: p50/p95 banding and measurement evidence for Hosted API

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear ask. A couple quick clarifications from our side before legal will sign off:

- The proposed +25% on p95 — is that relative to the contract baseline or to the prior 30-day observed p95?
- For the 7-day rolling window carveout, do you plan to exclude synthetic load (internal test traffic) from the measurement?

I'll share this with our Legal and SRE leads. If you can include the exact metric definition and a one-page sample of the measurement CSV we can circulate internally.

Sam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: p50/p95 banding and measurement evidence for Hosted API

Hannah / Marissa —

Attaching the evidence bundle. Notes below that you can paste into the addendum or send to Sam: see attached slo-evidence.zip (contains: measurement_method.md, sample_p95_report.csv, rolling_window_script.py, and dashboard_screenshots.png).

Short summary (to include in the addendum):
- Metric definitions: p50 and p95 are computed on per-request end-to-end server response time measured at the ingress edge (TLS termination) for the Hosted API route used by Brightline (route-id: brt-hrc-prod).
- Sampling & aggregation: We compute per-minute histograms and then aggregate into 5-minute windows. The p95 is computed on the concatenated sample set per rolling window; for contract enforcement we use a 7-day rolling window sampled every hour.
- Synthetic/excluded traffic: We exclude requests that present our internal x-test-traffic header and calls from known internal IP ranges (list in measurement_method.md).
- Evidence files: sample_p95_report.csv shows timestamps, token_count, latency_ms, and a column marking excluded requests.

Operational caveat: the +25% tolerance is applied to the contractual baseline p95 (the baseline is the average p95 over the 30 days immediately preceding the migration start date). If Brightline prefers baseline-to-baseline comparison (sliding baseline) we can propose alternate language but it requires a slightly different rollback trigger.

I included a small script that calculates the rolling 7-day percentile described above; ops can run it locally for verification.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: slo-evidence.zip

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Brightline Legal <legal@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: p50/p95 banding and measurement evidence for Hosted API

Sam — forwarding Karthik's note and the evidence bundle. I also attached a short draft addendum (redwood-draft-addendum.pdf) that:
- Defines baseline as the 30-day pre-migration p95;
- Applies a +25% tolerance to contractual p95 for any single 7-day rolling window during Dec 15–Jan 15;
- Excludes synthetic traffic and internal IP ranges from measurements;
- Includes an automatic rollback if p95 degrades beyond +50% for any 14-day sustained period.

If Legal is OK with that framing, please reply-all with approval language and Marissa will book a 30-minute ops sync to run through the verification script and handoff.

Links: hubspot deal and the evidence folder are here — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/2197 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dSLO-evidence

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah —

Thanks, this is exactly what Legal and SRE needed. Two small asks before we approve:

1) Can you change the wording so the +25% is "up to +25%" to make clear we remain accountable to return to baseline earlier if operational mitigation succeeds?
2) On the exclusion list, can you add our synthetic load JobID prefix (bright-synth-) so our CI traffic is explicitly excluded?

If you can confirm those two tweaks in writing, Legal will provide an explicit approval email and we'll sign the addendum. Once signed, please schedule the ops sync — Marissa, are you available next Tue at 10am PT?

Sam
